exceptions.reason: Only the outbound HTTP/2 client used by the network monitor and benchmark reporter is reachable; probe targets are operator-configured. Fixed by the Go 1.27.2 toolchain bump the release build adopts before this exception expires.
The reachable HTTP client only issues GET probes and never sends CONNECT, so the desynchronization sequence after a rejected CONNECT cannot be triggered. Fixed by the Go 1.27.2 toolchain bump.

No MWX-ISP listener configures Encrypted Client Hello, so the malformed ECH outer-extension path is not exercised by the EAP-TLS, RadSec or admin TLS handshakes. Fixed by the Go 1.27.2 toolchain bump.

The reachable multipart reader is the authenticated admin user-import endpoint, whose request body is capped at 16 MiB by middleware.BodyLimit and whose caller already holds tenant-wide write access. Fixed by the Go 1.27.2 toolchain bump.

Reachable only through net/http.ServeContent, which the admin server uses to serve the embedded UI to authenticated operators. The defect is availability-only and the fix ships with the Go 1.27.2 toolchain bump.
Reachable through the same outbound HTTP/2 client as GO-2026-6603: the network monitor probes operator-configured targets. Fixed by the Go 1.27.2 toolchain bump before this exception expires.

The reachable HTTP/2 server is the admin listener behind the operator network and reverse proxy; the impact is CPU availability, not confidentiality or integrity. Fixed by the Go 1.27.2 toolchain bump.
HTTP/2 flow-control refund defect on the admin listener; impact is availability of the management plane only. The standard-library fix ships with the Go 1.27.2 toolchain bump.
The admin router has no CONNECT or proxy handler, so no 2xx CONNECT response is ever produced and the desynchronization sequence is unreachable. Fixed by the Go 1.27.2 toolchain bump.
HPACK encoder race reachable only on the admin listener, where a crash costs management-plane availability until restart. Fixed by the Go 1.27.2 toolchain bump.

RadSec verifies peers against a deployment-configured CA bundle, so exploitation needs a compromised intermediate in that chain; the fix is the Go 1.27.3 distrust list adopted with the toolchain bump.
